title: M5 game-state simulator: pre-declared fitting, selection and validation rules
declared_before: any simulator run on the dev seasons (2023-24, 2024-25) or the holdout (2025-26)

seasons.scope: regular-season games (game type 02) with finite point-in-time inputs; playoffs are simulated live but not scored

inputs: point in time only: team / goalie state from games before the game date, RAPM v2 lineup term and FIN as of d - 2 days (committed lineup_features.csv.gz), league levels decayed over earlier games; the anchoring target is the live game model's walk-forward probability (folds trained on earlier seasons only) and goal_model.expected_total

markets.pl_home: home -1.5 on the official final (shootout goal included)
markets.tot60: over / push / under 6.0, multinomial log loss
markets.p1_2w: 1st period 2-way with ties refunded, scored on non-tied periods
markets.derivative_score: sum over the derivative set of the mean per-game log loss

rules.dispersion: fit seasons only: overall goal scale set so the mean simulated total equals the actual mean; Gamma shapes of the shared pace shock and the per-team shock chosen on a grid {0 (none), 60, 30, 15} x {0, 60, 30, 15} by the mean of log P(final total) + log P(final margin) - LL(reg 3-way) - LL(ML); scale refit once at the chosen shapes
rules.rest: the back-to-back terms (fitted on the fit seasons inside the 5v5 rate regression) stay only if, on the dev seasons pooled, removing them makes the raw simulator's ML log loss + derivative score worse (lower is better)
rules.anchoring: variant (a) raw simulator vs (b) simulator anchored (tilt + pace, bisection on likelihood-ratio weights) to the game model's walk-forward win probability and expected total; pick the lower derivative score on the dev seasons pooled; ties (|diff| < 0.0005) go to (b), which keeps the published moneyline coherent with every derivative price
rules.naive_baseline: goal_model independent Poisson with the same win % and expected total as the variant it is compared with (raw: the simulator's own; anchored: the game model's)
rules.holdout: one look at 2025-26 with the configuration fixed by the rules above, logged in bu/sim/out/look_log.jsonl; no parameter or rule changes after it; the holdout result is reported whatever it is
rules.publication: the simulator's probabilities for every derivative market are published (frozen pregame, graded by generate_history.py), but their EVs are INFO ONLY (never gate-open, no units) until the live test passes
rules.live_test: per market, on 2026-27 regular-season games with a frozen pregame model probability and a timestamped closing price (odds_close / snapshots): at least 300 graded games and model log loss <= de-vigged closing log loss + 0.002 with the sim also beating the naive Poisson on the same games; until then INFO ONLY

amendments.before: any dev / holdout run (none has been made)
amendments.change: rule 'dispersion' also fits a strength stretch s in {1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75} (every team-strength term of the four rate regressions multiplied by s; constants and home ice unchanged) on the same fit-season criterion, jointly with the shock shapes, grid {0, 60, 30, 15} (pace) x {0, 30} (team)
amendments.why: on the fit seasons the per-state regressions are each calibrated but the simulated margins are compressed (actual margin on simulated expected margin: slope 1.46; ML calibration slope 1.5): a team's strengths across states go together more than separate state regressions carry; diagnosed on the fit seasons only

amendments.before: any dev / holdout run (none has been made)
amendments.change: (1) a post-goal lull (goal hazards x m for the first 10 s and 10-30 s after any goal, m measured on the fit seasons' 5v5 time) is part of the structural fit; (2) the dispersion grid replaces the independent per-team Gamma shock by a game-level strength tilt: log home rates + e, log away rates - e, e ~ N(0, sd), sd in {0, 0.1, 0.2}; pace shock shape in {0 (none), 30}; stretch in {1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75}; same fit-season criterion
amendments.why: fit seasons: actual totals are under-dispersed (residual variance / mean 0.86, 1st-period variance / mean 0.96) and home / away goals are negatively correlated (-0.07), while the simulator had variance / mean 0.94-0.99 and no correlation; the measured lull (5v5 goal rate 0.17x in the 10 s after a goal, 0.79x in the next 20 s) brings the simulated 1st period to 0.96; independent team shocks and the pace shock both raise total variance, which the first grid points confirmed (criterion fell)
